subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw add this external-orchestrator lease and metadata contract as a core Gateway API, or require an owner plugin to use a narrower generic core seam?
rationale: The patch adds named external-product behavior, public RPC methods, persisted state, and authorization semantics across core boundaries; code review cannot safely choose the permanent public ownership model without maintainer product and API intent.

options.title: Define a generic core seam first
options.body: Keep only reusable lease-bound spawn primitives in core and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata vocabulary, and integration policy to the owning plugin or adapter.

options.title: Sponsor a core Gateway contract
options.body: Explicitly accept the public core API, then require a documented stable contract, upgrade-safe storage ensure, accurate generated catalog surface, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Keep it downstream
options.body: Close or pause this implementation if the downstream adapter can meet the need without expanding OpenClaw’s core public surface.

recommendation.title: Define a generic core seam first
recommendation.body: Keep only reusable lease-bound spawn primitives in core and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata vocabulary, and integration policy to the owning plugin or adapter.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence architecture-routing candidate for the core-versus-plugin API decision.
